agricultural: broad cultivated land with regular field texture and open farmland layout.
airplane: visible aircraft body with wings and tail, compact object-level structure, and clear airplane contours.
baseballdiamond: compact sports field with a distinct diamond-shaped infield.
beach: bright shoreline region with a clear sand-water boundary.
buildings: large roofed man-made structures with block-like geometry and organized built-up layout.
chaparral: irregular dry shrub-covered terrain with coarse natural texture and sparse woody vegetation.
denseresidential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal spacing.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with natural dark-green texture.
freeway: wide multi-lane transportation corridor with continuous road surface and branching traffic structure.
golfcourse: well-maintained green fairways with landscaped grass regions and designed open-course layout.
harbor: waterfront port area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent infrastructure.
intersection: road crossing region where multiple transportation lines meet.
mediumresidential: moderately spaced residential buildings with visible yards and balanced housing density.
mobilehomepark: repetitive small elongated housing units arranged in orderly rows.
overpass: elevated crossing transport structure with visible grade separation.
parkinglot: large open paved area with organized parking spaces and vehicle-oriented layout.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous channel shape and visible banks.
runway: long straight paved strip with elongated linear geometry and open surroundings.
sparseresidential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density.
storagetanks: large circular or cylindrical industrial containers with highly regular round geometry.
tenniscourt: small rectangular court surfaces with clear line markings and repeated sports-court geometry.
